source_text:
Καὶ πρῶτόν γε περὶ Διονυσίου φατέον· ὅτι τε τῆς ἐν Κορίνθῳ παροικίας τὸν τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς ἐγκεχείριστο θρόνον· καὶ ὡς τῆς ἐνθέου φιλοπονίας οὐ μόνον τοῖς ὑπ᾿ αὐτὸν, ἀλλ᾿ ἤδη καὶ τοῖς ἐπὶ τῆς ἀλλοδαπῆς ἀφθόνως ἐκοινώνει· χρησιμώτατον ἅποσιν ἑαυτὸν καθιστὰς, ἐν αἷς ὑπετυποῦτο καθολικαῖς πρὸς τὰς ἐκκλησίας ἐπιστολαῖς. ὧν ἐστιν, Ἡ ΜΕΝ ΠΡΟΣ ΛΑΚΕΔΑIΜΟΝΙΟΥΣ, ὀρθοδοξίας κατηχητικὴ, εἰρήνης τε καὶ ἑνώσεως ὑποθετική.
Ἡ ΔΕ ΠΡΟΣ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΟΥΣ, διεγερτικὴ πίστεως καὶ τῆς κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον πολιτείας· ἧς ὀλιγωρήσαντας ἐλέγχει, ὡς ἂν μικροῦ δεῖν ἀποστάντας τοῦ λόγου, ἐξ οὗπερ τὸν προεστῶτα αὐτῶν Πούπλιον μαρτυρῆσαι κατὰ τοὺς τότε συνέβη διωγμούς. Κοδράτου δὲ μετὰ τὸν μαρτυρήσαντα Πούπλιον καταστάντος αὐτῶν ἐπισκόπου μέμνηται· ἐπιμαρτυρῶν, ὡς ἂν διὰ τῆς αὐτοῦ σπουδῆς ἐπισυναχθέντων, καὶ τῆς πίστεως ἀναζωπύρησιν εἰληχότων· δηλοῖ δ᾿ ἐπὶ τούτοις, ὡς καὶ Διονύσιος ὁ Ἀρεοπαγίτης ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀποστόλου Παύλου προτραπεὶς ἐπὶ τὴν πίστιν κατὰ τὰ ἐν ταῖς πράξεσι δεδηλωμένα, πρῶτος τῆς ἐν Ἀθήναις παροικίας τὴν ἐπισκοπὴν ἐγκεχείριστο.
Ἄλλη δ᾿ ἐπιστολή τις αὐτοῦ ΠΡΟΣ ΝΙΚΟΜΗΔΕΑΣ φέρεται· ἐν τὴν Μαρκίωνος αἵρεσιν πολεμῶν, τῷ τῆς ἀληθείας παρίσταται κανόνι.
Καὶ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ δὲ τῇ παροικούσῃ ΓΟΡΤΥΝΑΝ ἉΜΑ ΤΑΙΣ ΛΟΙΠΑΙΣ ΚΑΤΑ ΚΡΗΤΗΝ ΠΑΡΟΙΚΙΑΙΣ ἐπιστείλας, Φίλιππον ἐπίσκοπον αὐτῶν ἀποδέχεται, ἅτε δὴ ἐπὶ πλείσταις μαρτυρουμένης ἀνδραγαθίαις τῆς ὑπ᾿ αὐτὸν ἐκκλησίας· τήν τε τῶν αἱρετικῶν διαστροφὴν ὑπομιμνήσκει φυλάττεσθαι.
Καὶ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ δὲ τῇ παροικούσῃ ΑΜΑΣΤΡΙΝ ἉΜΑ ΤΑΙΣ ΚΑΤΑ ΠΟΝΤΟΝ ἐπιστείλας, Βακχυλίδου μὲν καὶ Ἐλπίστου, ὡς ἂν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ γράψαι προτρεψάντων μέμνηται· γραφῶν τε θείων ἐξηγήσεις παρατέθειται· ἐπίσκοπον αὐτῶν ὀνόματι Πάλμαν ὑποσημαίνων· πολλὰ δὲ περὶ γάμου καὶ ἁγνείας τοῖς αὐτοῖς παραινεῖ. καὶ τοὺς ἐξ οἵας δ᾿ οὖν ἀποπτώσεως, εἴτε πλημμελείας, εἴτε μὴν αἱρετικῆς πλάνης ἐπιστρέφοντας, δεξιοῦσθαι προστάττει.
Ταύταις ἄλλη ἐγκατείλεκται ΠΡΟΣ ΚΝΩΣΣΙΟΥΣ ἐπιστολὴ, ἐν ᾗ Πινυτὸν τῆς παροικίας ἐπίσκοπον παρακαλεῖ, μὴ βαρὺ φορτίον ἐπάναγκες τὸ περὶ ἁγνείας τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἐπιτιθέναι, τῆς δὲ τῶν πολλῶν καταστοχάζεσθαι ἀσθενείας.—
Καὶ ἄλλη δέ τις παρὰ ταύτας ἐπιστολὴ τοῦ Διονυσίου φέρεται, ΧΡΥΣΟΦΟΡΑ πιστοτάτῃ ἀδελφῇ ἐπιστείλαντος. ᾗ τὰ κατάλληλα γράφων, τῆς προσηκούσης καὶ αὐτῇ μετεδίδου λογικῆς τροφῆς.
orientation: Eusebius is cataloguing the surviving letters of Dionysius of Corinth, summarizing the occasion and content of each.
pass_a_gloss: And first indeed concerning Dionysius it must be said: that he had been entrusted with the throne of the office of bishop of the church in Corinth; and that he shared the inspired diligence abundantly not only with those under him, but already also with those in foreign parts, making himself most useful to all in the catholic letters to the churches which he composed. Of which there is: the one to the Lacedaemonians, catechetical of orthodoxy and suggestive of peace and unity. The one to the Athenians, stirring up of faith and of the conduct according to the gospel; he convicts them of having neglected it, as having almost departed from the word, from the time when it happened that their leader Publius was martyred during the persecutions of that time. He mentions Quadratus, who was appointed their bishop after Publius who was martyred; testifying that through his zeal they were gathered together and received a rekindling of faith; he shows in addition to these things that Dionysius the Areopagite, having been turned to the faith by the apostle Paul according to the things declared in the Acts, was the first to be entrusted with the office of bishop of the church in Athens. And another letter of his to the Nicomedians is extant, in which he fights against the heresy of Marcion, he stands by the standard of truth. And having written to the church dwelling in Gortyn together with the rest of the churches in Crete, he accepts Philip their bishop, since indeed the church under him is testified to for very many deeds of manly virtue; and he reminds them to guard against the distortion of the heretics. And having written to the church dwelling in Amastris together with the churches in Pontus, he mentions Bacchylides and Elpistus, as having urged him to write; and he sets forth explanations of the divine writings; indicating their bishop by name Palmas; and he advises them much concerning marriage and purity. And he commands them to receive kindly those who turn back from any kind of fall, whether of transgression or indeed of heretical error. To these another letter to the Cnossians is included, in which he exhorts Pinytus, bishop of the church, not to impose a heavy compulsory burden concerning purity on the brethren, but to aim at the weakness of the many. And another letter besides these of Dionysius is extant, he having written to Chrysophora, a most faithful sister. Writing to her the fitting things, he shared with her also the spiritual food that was proper.

choices.english: had been entrusted with the throne of the office of bishop
choices.why: Keeps the literal 'throne' (θρόνος) and the glossary rendering 'office of bishop' for ἐπισκοπή, preserving the source's concrete image of episcopal succession.
rejected: had been given the episcopal seat

choices.why: ἔνθεος means 'inspired' or 'divinely filled'; rendering it as 'inspired' keeps the adjective's force without over-translating.
Uses the glossary's 'orthodoxy' for ὀρθοδοξία and keeps the adjective 'catechetical' literal, preserving the instructional character of the letter.

choices.english: of the conduct according to the gospel
choices.why: πολιτεία means 'way of life' or 'conduct'; rendering it as 'conduct' keeps the ethical sense while 'according to the gospel' preserves the prepositional phrase.
rejected: of the evangelical way of life

choices.english: he stands by the standard of truth
choices.why: Uses the glossary's 'standard of truth' for κανὼν τῆς ἀληθείας and renders παρίσταται as 'stands by' to keep the verb's sense of taking a position alongside.
rejected: he adheres to the rule of truth
he aligns with the canon of truth

choices.why: Uses the glossary's 'spiritual food' for λογικὴ τροφή, avoiding the literal 'rational food' which would mislead in English.

pass_b_english: First, then, we must speak about Dionysius: he had been entrusted with the throne of the office of bishop of the church in Corinth, and he shared his inspired diligence generously not only with those under him but already with those in foreign lands as well. He made himself most useful to all through the catholic letters he composed to the churches. Among these is the one to the Lacedaemonians, catechetical of orthodoxy and urging peace and unity.

The one to the Athenians stirs up faith and the conduct according to the gospel. He rebukes them for having neglected this, since they had almost fallen away from the word after their leader Publius happened to be martyred during the persecutions of that time. He mentions that Quadratus became their bishop after Publius was martyred, testifying that through his zeal they were gathered together and received a rekindling of faith. He also makes clear that Dionysius the Areopagite, having been turned to the faith by the apostle Paul according to what is shown in the Acts, was the first to be entrusted with the office of bishop of the church in Athens.
Another letter of his is addressed to the people of Nicomedia, in which he fights against the heresy of Marcion and stands by the standard of truth.

Writing also to the church that sojourns in Gortyn together with the rest of the churches in Crete, he accepts Philip their bishop, since the church under him is testified to for very many deeds of courage. He also reminds them to guard against the distortion of the heretics.

Writing to the church that sojourns in Amastris together with the churches in Pontus, he mentions Bacchylides and Elpistus as having urged him to write. He sets out explanations of the divine writings and indicates their bishop by the name of Palmas. He gives much advice to them about marriage and purity, and he commands them to welcome those who turn back from any fall whatever, whether from transgression or from heretical error.

Among these is included another letter to the people of Cnossus, in which he urges Pinytus, bishop of the church, not to impose a heavy burden of compulsory purity on the brethren, but to take into account the weakness of the many.

And another letter of Dionysius besides these is preserved, written to Chrysophora, a most faithful sister. Writing to her what was fitting, he gave her a share of the spiritual food that was proper for her as well.

last_rejected.quote: He made himself most useful to all through the catholic letters he composed to the churches.
last_rejected.source_quote: χρησιμώτατον ἅπασιν ἑαυτὸν καθιστὰς, ἐν αἷς ὑπετυποῦτο καθολικαῖς πρὸς τὰς ἐκκλησίας ἐπιστολαῖς.
last_rejected.why: Source says 'to all' (ἅπασιν), not 'to all through'; letters are 'among which' (ἐν αἷς) he was outlined, not 'through which' he made himself useful.
last_rejected.fix: making himself most useful to all, among which he was outlined in catholic letters to the churches.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek says he made himself most useful to all, and in the letters he excelled; English paraphrases as 'through the letters', preserving meaning.

problems.why: Same place named two ways; reader may not connect them.
problems.fix: Note Lacedaemonians = Spartans at first occurrence.

problems.quote: First, then, we must speak about Dionysius
problems.why: Speaker is Eusebius, not Dionysius; shift unmarked.
Odd English; likely 'instructive in' or 'teaching orthodoxy.'
Odd phrasing; likely 'enforced continence' or 'strict chastity.'

fixed: Sparta: The English uses 'Lacedaemonians' consistently with the source ΛΑΚΕΔΑIΜΟΝΙΟΥΣ; no 'Sparta' appears, so no edit needed.
Speaker: The English 'First, then, we must speak about Dionysius' is Eusebius's narrative voice, as in the source; no shift is marked in the source, so no edit needed.

Mistranslation 'catechetical of orthodoxy': The source κατηχητικὴ means 'instructive' or 'catechetical'; 'catechetical of orthodoxy' is awkward English, so changed to 'instructive concerning orthodoxy'.

Mistranslation 'compulsory purity': The source ἐπάναγκες τὸ περὶ ἁγνείας means 'a compulsory burden concerning purity'; 'compulsory purity' is awkward, so changed to 'enforced strictness regarding purity'.
